answer: An identity that attests to another stakes 20% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. The atlas escrow holds each stake, the grove settlement releases it, and the wharf audit lists every transfer. A farm running 53 keys thus pays that exposure 53 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
